textual.observation: A free Target gift card is advertised alongside an instruction to visit coke.com.
textual.context: Promotional context is suggested by the title and description, but the source records do not establish whether the visit is required to receive the gift card or explain the relationship between Target and coke.com.
textual.potential_relevance: The observed free-gift-card claim is paired with a requested visit to an external destination, requiring later assessment of the offer terms and whether the destination matches the promised benefit.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish eligibility, fulfillment terms, fees, data requests, destination ownership, or whether the gift card offer is genuine. No video context is available beyond the supplied records.

visual.observation: The slide presents a "$2 Target eGift Card" as a reward for Coke Rewards account members who log in, open the Rewards tab, locate the stated offer, and enter or scan four Coke codes.
visual.context: The content is shown as promotional instructions for a Coke Rewards offer and states that participation is free to join.
visual.potential_relevance: A promised gift card is directly linked to account access, navigating to a specific offer, and submitting or scanning multiple codes, which is a task-relevant reward-and-action relationship.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish whether the offer is authentic, whether any account information beyond login is requested, whether codes are submitted successfully, or whether the gift card is delivered.

visual.observation: The stated reward is only unlocked after 50,000 eligible accounts participate, and the viewer is told to log in and claim it within five days after unlocking or it will disappear.
visual.context: The participation threshold and five-day claim condition are presented as terms of the promotional offer.
visual.potential_relevance: The reward is tied to a large participation threshold and a time-limited claim instruction, creating a notable condition-and-urgency relationship relevant to further review.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not establish whether the threshold is reached, whether the deadline is enforced, or what occurs after the stated period.

visual_context_notes.observation: The opening slide visibly uses Target branding and the title "Free Target Gift Card!!!".
The closing slide asks viewers to like, share, and subscribe.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents couponing and rewards guidance centered on a free-to-join Coke Rewards offer for a $2 Target eGift Card after entering four Coke codes and meeting the stated participation threshold. The described urgency and reward conditions are part of the promotion, while no fee, private credential request beyond account login, promised profit, impersonation, or unsupported transaction outcome by the creator is described. The like, share, subscribe request and separate referral links are characterized as ordinary engagement or shopping-rewards references rather than requirements for the offer.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary subject is an ordinary rewards promotion: a Target eGift Card is presented as a conditional benefit within a Coke Rewards participation flow involving account access and entry of Coke codes.

evidence.observation: The frame visibly presents a Coke Rewards offer for account members, states that a $2 Target eGift Card is associated with entering four Coke codes, and lists account-login, offer-navigation, code-entry, and claim instructions.
The frame visibly states that the reward is unlocked when 50,000 eligible accounts participate and that the unlocked reward must be claimed within 5 days or it will disappear.
The title advertises a free Target gift card.
The description pairs the gift-card promotion with an instruction to visit coke.com.
